source.title: Mammo-SAE: Interpreting Breast Cancer Concept Learning with Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study probes and intervenes on sparse-autoencoder features in a medical vision-language model, and evaluates whether those features preserve task information. It does not use the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE reconstruction performance, interventions on selected latent neurons, and concept-localization measurements. It does not test superposition geometry, feature competition for dimensions, or feature behavior in LLMs. Table 2 reports mAP separately for each top-10 neuron; those measurements are retained as separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains one SAE on the final-layer features of a mammography CNN/CLIP model (EfficientNet-B5 backbone) as an interpretability tool. It reports domain findings: concept-aligned latents, confounding background latents and finetuning effects. It does not test superposition, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality. V4 names LLMs, and this is a vision model. For V5, it never asks whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical: there is one SAE, one seed, one dictionary size and no comparison across dictionaries. The reconstruction-AUC check is a fidelity check of the tool, not a test of the units claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE latents in Mammo-CLIP include clinically aligned neurons and also background or confounding neurons, and that finetuning sharpens class separation in latent space. They state the finetuned model 'consistently' has higher mAP. Table 2 contradicts this for some ranks: calcification ranks 2-4 (0.007 vs 0.053-0.085) and mass ranks 5, 6 and 8 (0.0 vs about 0.02).
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a patch-level SAE on Mammo-CLIP visual features and probes and intervenes on its latents; it does not apply the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports differences between pretrained and finetuned variants and between the mass and suspicious-calcification concepts. It analyzes only the final layer.

fits_no_version.finding: In a mammography vision model, an SAE (h=16,384) trained on final-layer features keeps downstream AUC within about 2%. Retaining only about 10 class-selected latents nearly recovers AUC in some settings, and deactivating more than 10 sharply lowers it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries recover sparse, task-sufficient latent features in vision (non-LLM) models.

fits_no_version.finding: The same latents (e.g., 13867, 15699) appear in the top-10 for both mass and calcification. Latent 15699 is strongly active for both classes and tracks background, so top SAE latents are not concept-specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Top class-selected SAE latents in vision models can be shared across concepts or respond to spurious regions.

record.problems: Only one medical vision-language model and its pretrained/finetuned variants are studied; analysis is limited to the final layer and two concepts. No uncertainty estimates or null controls are reported. The intervention curves are presented in a figure without exact tabulated values, and the paper does not test feature completeness, canonicality, or stability across independent dictionaries.

untested.parts: No toy models, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity. Polysemanticity is cited only as motivation.
No LLMs are studied. A dictionary is applied to a vision CNN, with no evidence about LLM feature spread.
Completeness, stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, and canonicality are all untested. Only one SAE was trained.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'tested' status and labels should be dropped. Reconstruction fidelity and top-k interventions on a single SAE do not address completeness, stability or canonicality, as the reader's own untested_parts admits. The system is a vision CNN, not an LLM, so V4 does not apply. Design caveat: one SAE was trained on the finetuned calcification model and reused everywhere, which confounds the pretrained-versus-finetuned comparisons. There are no uncertainty estimates or controls, and only the final layer is analysed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy-network superposition, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition, or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
Studies a mammography vision-language model, not LLMs; it does not assess whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recoverable by a dictionary.

Tests whether SAE latents preserve task information and exhibit concept-related behavior, but not whether the features are complete, uniquely canonical, or stable across independent dictionaries and training runs.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Mammo-CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared prediction AUC-ROC using original features with SAE-reconstructed features
rows.note: The reported AUC-ROC is lower with SAE-reconstructed features.
rows.check: SAE reconstruction-fidelity check, not a test of V5's complete/stable/canonical claim. The SAE was trained only on finetuned calcification-model features and then reused on the pretrained model. The 0.951 to 0.933 drop therefore reflects cross-model transfer of one SAE, not SAE incompleteness on its own training model.

rows.subject: Mammo-CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared prediction AUC-ROC using original features with SAE-reconstructed features
rows.note: The SAE-reconstructed features retain approximately the reported original predictive performance.
rows.check: Fidelity check of the tool (0.978 vs 0.979). This is the model the SAE was trained on. It does not bear on canonicality or stability.

rows.check: Same issue as r1: the SAE was trained on finetuned calcification features and transferred to the pretrained model for the mass task (0.786 to 0.763).

rows.subject: Mammo-CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Retained only top-k class-specific SAE neurons and zeroed the others

conditions.value: as few as 10; k varied up to h = 16,384

rows.note: The text says as few as 10 neurons nearly recover the original AUC-ROC in multiple cases, without identifying those cases in the description.
rows.check: Top-k retention intervention, read from a figure only. It shows task signal concentrated in a few latents, not whether features are canonical units. The text says only 'multiple cases', not which.

rows.subject: Mammo-CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the top-k class-specific SAE neurons while leaving other latent activations unchanged
rows.note: The text reports a sharp AUC-ROC drop when more than 10 selected neurons are deactivated, but does not identify the affected cases individually.
rows.check: Top-k deactivation intervention, read from a figure only. It measures reliance on selected latents and does not bear on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-reconstructed features and selected-neuron interventions on Mammo-CLIP
reader_labels.reason: Reconstructed features retain near-original AUC-ROC in the reported comparisons, and selected SAE latents have reported effects on task AUC; see r2, r4, r5, and r6.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Reconstruction lowers AUC-ROC for both pretrained concepts, and localization results vary substantially by concept, variant, and neuron; these measures do not establish complete or canonical units; see r1, r3, and r7–r46.
